product: Coca-Cola — a fan-made Grok-generated retro ad (not an official ad).
body: A fan used Grok to generate a retro-style Coca-Cola ad in about a minute, then dubbed in music via TikTok — pitched as a demo of users making ads for brands. 20s video attached; @CocaCola, @nikitabier, and @elonmusk tagged.
idea: AI lets anyone make a retro brand ad in a minute — fans become the creative department.
sequencing: "Made you a retro ad in a minute."
why_it_works: Retro aesthetics are instantly recognizable and cheap for AI to mimic.
what_to_steal: The speed — LC retro infomercials can be generated in minutes, not produced in weeks.

product: commentary — no product. The AI pharmacist authority-figure ad format ($5, 4 minutes).
hook: "ai pharmacists are the most underrated ad format right now."
body: Generate an AI pharmacist, write the script, paste it in — 30-second video out the other side for $5 in about 4 minutes; jokes a real pharmacist wouldn't do it for $5,000. 26s video attached (transcript is a fragment: "take the zero sugar goly best seller trio").
idea: AI authority figures collapse expert-endorsement production to $5 and 4 minutes.
why_it_works: White-coat authority transfers trust instantly; AI removes the cost and compliance friction of real experts.
what_to_steal: The $5/4-minute authority production model for LC — an AI "jewelry expert" explaining plating vs PVD.

product: Poo-Pourri — retro-styled static ad (the post is commentary on their creative).
hook: "this static is weird enough to make you stop."
body: Poo-Pourri wrapped an awkward product (toilet spray) in a polished retro ad; the contrast is the mechanism: classy visual, awkward problem, simple promise, memorable brand. Photo attached. (Post truncated.)
idea: Classy retro visuals plus an awkward problem equals memorable contrast.
why_it_works: Contrast — the visual promises class, the problem delivers awkwardness; the tension is memorable.
what_to_steal: The contrast formula for LC: classy retro visual + the awkward problem (green neck, faded jewelry) + simple promise (never fades).

product: BESK — botanical oil for aging skin (7 botanicals; 550,000+ women; for women 40+); the post is commentary on the retro format with the ad video attached.
hook: "15 years as a dermatologist" plus the 1987 daytime-TV aesthetic.
body: A dermatologist in a pink blazer delivers a daytime-TV-style recommendation: most moisturizers are 70% water that evaporates by noon; aging skin needs botanical oils that absorb beneath the surface; BESK's 7 botanicals visibly improve skin over time; 550,000+ women; direct close ("what are you waiting for?").
cta: "So, what are you waiting for?" (implied shop CTA).
idea: Un-polished 1987 daytime-TV authority — the retro format itself is the scroll-stopper.
formatting: 48s vertical video (720x1280); retro daytime-TV aesthetic, pink blazer.
why_it_works: The retro format is so out of place in a polished DTC feed that it stops the scroll; then classic authority plus mechanism plus proof closes.
what_to_steal: The full skeleton for LC: "20 years as a jeweler" + retro TV aesthetic + mechanism (plating vs PVD) + proof + direct close.

product: An unnamed US supplement brand — 3.17x ROAS creative/account breakdown ($34k spend → $108k revenue, 28 days).
hook: "Supplement brand, US market only. Last 28 days: $34,126 spent, $108,242 back, 3.17x average across the account."
body: Account structure: 1 CBO per product, 1 ad set per persona. Working creatives: Suno AI ads, professor interviews, FaceTime calls, native ads, WhatsApp conversations, AI short movies. Two photos attached.
idea: Simple account structure (CBO × product, ad set × persona) plus format-diverse creative equals 3.17x.
sequencing: Creatives: Suno AI, prof interviews, FaceTime calls, native ads, WhatsApp conversations, AI short movies.
why_it_works: Persona-level ad sets let each creative speak to one buyer; professor interviews supply authority cheaply.
what_to_steal: "Professor interviews" as LC's expert-authority creative — interview a materials/jewelry expert on camera.
